speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Varicella (Chickenpox) secondary infection or concurrent outbreak.

The cluster of painless papules on the abdomen in a 2-year-old with a brother who had chickenpox one month ago and daycare exposure is highly suggestive of a new Varicella infection or a secondary bacterial infection like impetigo given the daycare context. Given the normal CBC, systemic infection is less likely, but the contact history is critical. We have reached the question limit. The diagnosis is Varicella.
